about.title: A live network for ideas, products, and performance.
paragraphs: SYNAPTRA '26 is the flagship symposium of the Department of Computer Science and Business Systems at Syed Ammal Engineering College. The name joins synapse and the year’s charge: a day when student work is presented, tested, and connected in public.

The programme is deliberately mixed. Technical floors cover paper presentation, project expo, and UI/UX design. Non-technical floors cover quiz and auction. Participants leave with critique, visibility, and a record of having competed on a formal campus stage.
about.quote: CSBS sits between computing and business systems. SYNAPTRA is built for that overlap — rigorous enough for research, open enough for product, design, and strategy.
pillars: Frame a problem with evidence — a paper, a product thesis, or a design brief.
Show the work: slides, a prototype, a flow, or a live demonstration.
Meet a jury and a room. Technical and non-technical tracks run the same day.
Take feedback, meet peers from other campuses, and convert the day into a next step.

eventsIntro.title: Five events. One campus day.
eventsIntro.lead: Choose a primary event at registration. Open a brief for format, evaluation focus, and what to bring. Final slot lists are issued to registered participants.

events.title: Paper Presentation
events.blurb: Pitch a unique SDG idea on 6–9 slides. Include the required titles. Teams of 1–4. 5–7 minutes.

events.title: Project Expo
events.blurb: A 1–4 member team shows an original, SDG-aligned build. Preferred: working demo and a 6–8 slide intro.

events.title: UI/UX Design
events.blurb: A timed problem-statement sprint: map the user, design the flow, and ship a clear, original interface.

events.title: Quiz
events.blurb: Multiple timed rounds. Register before the start, report early, and leave gadgets at the desk.

events.title: Business Idea Auction
events.blurb: Pitch a business on slides, take investment offers, and negotiate — keep more than 50% ownership.

paper.lead: Present a unique idea before a faculty jury. Keep the deck visual and align the work to any of the 17 SDGs. Teams of 1–4.
format: Maximum 6–9 slides, including the title slide. Team size is 1–4 members.
The six required titles must appear in the PPT, in that order.
Avoid paragraphs. Use points, diagrams, infographics, or pictures.
Keep the explanation precise. The idea should satisfy any of the 17 SDG goals.
The idea must be unique and novel. Each team has 5–7 minutes to present.
Upload a PPT only — no Word or other formats.
paper.bring: Laptop or the submitted PPT on a drive, and college ID.

expo.lead: Show an original project that solves a real-world problem and fits the SDGs. A working prototype is preferred. Walk the jury through the problem, the stack, the build, and the outcome.
format: Each team may have 1–4 members.
Projects must address a real-world problem and satisfy the SDG goals.
A 6–8 slide deck is preferred to introduce the core idea, problem statement, and methodology.
Original work only. A working prototype or demo is preferred.
7 minutes for presentation + 3 minutes for Q&A. Internet is subject to venue availability.
eval: Explain the problem, technology used, implementation, and outcome.
At least 80% of the project must be the participants' own work. AI tools must stay under 20%.
expo.bring: Laptop, demo hardware, chargers, required files, college ID, and a 6–8 slide deck if you have one.

uiux.lead: A timed design heat. You work from the assigned problem statement — identify the user, map the flow, then deliver a simple, readable interface. Craft matters; copying an existing product does not.
format: Read the problem fully before you draw. Design only for that brief; do not change the core requirement.
Name the target user and design for their needs. Lock a clear user flow before you finish the UI.
Keep screens simple, readable, and consistent. Show empty, error, success, and loading states where they matter.
Original work only. Figma or another permitted tool. Finish inside the given time.
eval: The time limit is closed. Work only on the assigned problem. No templates or copied products.
Internet, references, and AI only if announced before the heat. Disclose AI use if it is allowed.
Late submission may be penalised or dropped. The jury's decision is final.
submit: Final file or share link with the organisers before the deadline
uiux.bring: Laptop with Figma or your permitted tool, exported screens as backup, and college ID.

quiz.lead: Open to all eligible, registered participants. The quiz runs in multiple rounds. Each question has a clock. Answer inside it. The Quiz Master's call is final.
format: Every team or participant must register before the quiz begins.
Report at the venue 15 minutes before the scheduled time.
No phones, smart watches, gadgets, internet, or discussion unless the Quiz Master permits it.
eval: Malpractice means immediate disqualification. Maintain discipline throughout.
Rules and scoring may change by round and will be announced before that round starts.
Winners are decided on the final score. Prizes follow that ranking. The Quiz Master's decision is final.
quiz.bring: College ID and your team. Leave phones and wearables off the floor.

auction.lead: Pitch a business or product to the floor, take investment offers, and negotiate the equity. A physical prototype is optional. The team that lands the strongest capital while keeping the most ownership wins.
format: Present the idea or product on a PPT. A physical prototype is optional.
After the pitch, investors may offer money for a share of the business.
Accept, reject, or counter. The team must keep more than 50% ownership.
eval: The winner is the strongest investment amount with the highest ownership still held.
Pitch and negotiation must finish inside the given time.
No fake claims, plagiarism, or cheating. The judges' decision is final.
auction.bring: Laptop or a PPT on a drive, college ID, and a prototype only if you have one.

venue.title: Venue & arrival
venue.lead: SYNAPTRA '26 is hosted at the EEE Seminar Hall, Syed Ammal Engineering College (Autonomous), Ramanathapuram. Report at least 15 minutes before your first slot with a valid college identity card and your SYN registration ID.
points: Campus: Dr. E.M. Abdullah Campus, Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu
Host: Department of Computer Science and Business Systems
Dress: Formal or smart campus attire recommended for jury events
card: Ramanathapuram is connected by road and rail across southern Tamil Nadu. Use the college main gate and follow on-campus boards to the EEE block / seminar hall.
Inter-college participants should plan arrival before 08:30 so verification does not cut into the inaugural session.

rules.title: Registration
items: Online registration is mandatory before 23:59 IST on 13 October 2026.
The published fee is ₹200 per participant (per head), not per team.
Carry your college ID and the SYN ID issued after this form (or the official confirmation once the department form is linked).
Payment mode on campus, if required, will be confirmed by the organising committee.

rules.title: Eligibility & teams
items: Open to students of recognised institutions. SAEC students and visiting campuses are welcome.
Register a primary event. Additional entries are subject to slot availability and coordinator approval.
Team composition, where allowed, will be confirmed in the event brief and on-desk instructions.
All members listed must be present for judged rounds unless the coordinator records an exception.

rules.title: Time, discipline & campus
items: Report 15–30 minutes before your scheduled heat.
Late arrival may forfeit the slot. The jury will not restart a completed heat.
Follow allotted presentation, demo, and round durations.
College property, labs, and hall equipment are to be used only as directed.

rules.title: Originality, judging & conduct
items: Papers, projects, designs, and media must be the participants’ own work. Plagiarism or ghost entries mean disqualification.
Evaluation uses predefined technical and presentation criteria. Jury and coordinator decisions are final.
Professional conduct is required throughout. Harassment, disruption, or unsafe behaviour ends participation.

faqs.a: Undergraduate students from recognised colleges. CSBS hosts the day; other departments and campuses may enter any listed event.

faqs.q: Is the fee per team or per person?
faqs.a: The registration fee is ₹200 per participant for students from other colleges.

faqs.q: Can I enter more than one event?
faqs.a: Yes. You can take part in more than one event as long as the schedules do not clash.

faqs.q: Do I need to submit an abstract or prototype in advance?
faqs.a: No. You do not need to submit an abstract or prototype in advance for Paper Presentation or Project Expo. Register and present on the day of the event.
Food details will be shared in your registration confirmation.
Scan the QR code on the official poster, or use the Register button on this website.
Technical: Paper Presentation, Project Expo, and UI/UX Design. Non-technical: Quiz and Auction.
16 October 2026. Attractive prizes await the winners.
